findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing file, permission errors, or invalid UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: entire program aborts with panic when the data file is absent, unreadable, or contains malformed UTF-8, instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and propagate with ? or explicit map_err for typed I/O failure

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs console I/O inside the parsing/mapping closure
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic is no longer pure or deterministic; output ordering affects behavior, tests become order-dependent, and the shell/functional boundary is violated
findings.fix: move all logging/metrics to the imperative shell layer; the parsing closure must be a pure function with no I/O side effects

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses index 0 without bounds validation on split result
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with zero commas panics via IndexOut ofBounds instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and pattern match on (name, value_str) to avoid indexing entirely

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses index 1 without bounds validation on split result
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with only one comma (trailing comma, no value) panics via IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and pattern match to get the value side; no indexing needed

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value strings
findings.failure_mode: any non-integer field value (e.g. "abc", "3.14", empty) causes a panic rather than returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: return Result and use .map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue)? to convert parse failures into typed errors

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, corrupting data without any error or warning; a value like 70000 becomes 4463
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) or parse directly as u16: .parse::<u16>().map_err(...)? to fail on out-of-range values instead of silently truncating

findings.problem: load_packets fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), parsing, validation, and collection into a single function with no separation of concerns
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation; I/O failures are indistinguishable from parse errors; the function is not reusable in contexts where input comes from a different source
findings.fix: split into (1) a pure parse_packet(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for core logic and (2) a shell function that handles file I/O, delegates to parse_packet, and handles typed errors

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no Result type; all failures are expressed through panics rather than typed errors
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish between file-not-found, parse-invalid, parse-out-of-range, and other error classes; no structured error recovery is possible
findings.fix: define a ParseError enum with variants (e.g., IoError, EmptyLine, InvalidName, InvalidValue, Overflow) and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: no max_items cap, no try_reserve, and no bound on the number of lines or per-line Vec allocations
findings.failure_mode: a large or adversarial file can trigger unbounded memory allocation leading to OOM or denial of service with no cap enforcement
findings.fix: add a max_items parameter, validate lines against it before allocation, create Vec::new() with try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?, and enforce the cap during iteration

findings.problem: raw primitive String from file I/O crosses the parse boundary directly into Record construction without fallible smart constructor validation
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct invalid domain states (out-of-range values, empty names, non-numeric content) because the parse boundary has no validation gate
findings.fix: create a ParseError enum and a parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> smart constructor that validates name non-emptiness and value range before constructing Record

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec for a two-field CSV grammar
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary intermediate allocation per line; also silently accepts lines with more than one comma, silently ignoring extra fields
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to get (name, value_str) directly with a single allocation

findings.problem: parts: Vec<String> allocates a new Vec and clones every field per line
findings.failure_mode: quadratic allocation pattern for large files; each line creates two String allocations and one Vec allocation
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get &str parts and parse directly without intermediate Vec or String allocations

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for any performance claim about load_packets throughput or memory usage
findings.failure_mode: performance characteristics are unknown; claims about speed, memory, or scalability cannot be verified or regressed against
findings.fix: add a criterion or divan benchmark for load_packets with a realistic file, report baseline throughput and allocation count, and set a regression threshold

no second-ring evidence for any performance or safety claims

residual_risk: Static review identified 12 findings including 10 blockers: multiple panic surfaces (unwrap on I/O, parse, and indexing), lossy as conversion silently truncating values, hidden console I/O in pure parsing logic, fused shell/core violating functional boundaries, no typed error taxonomy, no resource bounds or try_reserve, and missing parse boundary validation. All unwrap/expect/panic surfaces must be replaced with typed Result propagation before any delivery. The function as written will abort on any malformed input, missing file, or out-of-range value. No commands were executed; verification gate (cargo fmt, check, clippy, test) must be run to confirm compilation state.
